rationale: Isaiah 54:9 (BSB) names 'the days of Noah' directly and recalls an oath 'that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth,' applying that oath to a different, later situation (the exile) without using a citation formula. Graded allusion rather than quotation because Isaiah paraphrases the oath in his own words rather than quoting Genesis verbatim; graded strong rather than explicit because named commentators disagree about which verse the oath most precisely echoes -- Barnes' Notes ties it to Genesis 8:21-22's own wording and the fact that the promise there 'had been kept,' while Ellicott's Commentary ties the 'covenant' language instead to 9:11, just past this lesson's own passage boundary. Both anchors are real and named; this connection is authored from 8:21-22 because that is where the promise's content first appears in the narrative this lesson covers, not because the dispute over the more precise anchor is resolved.
